- A short list of APIs/features that require entitlements or contract-level enablement (we called these "gated" in the call).

Hi Megan — thanks for the clear summary. Putting the short answers up front and then a proposed next step: 

Short answers:
- We currently gate three capability areas for marketplace listings: cross-tenant data export, server-side long-lived key provisioning, and admin-level prompt-moderation hooks.
- There is a potential de-gate milestone for the admin moderation hooks in Q4 (target Nov 2028) pending a compliance sweep; the other two items are tied to policy/legal changes and may need an exemption for partners.
- Exemption path: a joint security questionnaire + an attestation that partner maintains data segregation. We can produce an evidence pack (SOC snippets, audit log extract guidance).

Proposed next step: Karthik / Ben — can you review the attached matrix and suggest which APIs we could reasonably make exempt-by-request for CloudLane vs. which are long-term gated? I propose a short MOP (mutual action plan) with timeline blocks for legal and security sign-off.

Megan — I'll sync a MOP draft and a short doc with the sample evidence CloudLane would need. Can we lock a 30-min working session next week (your availability Tue/Thu morning PT)?

Evelyn Hart

Quick technical read: I skimmed the matrix (attached) and annotated which endpoints are tied to infra-level controls vs. policy-only gates. In short: 

- Cross-tenant data export is infra-gated (requires tenant-scoped isolation and audit logging) — we can support an exemption but it requires a short Dedicated capacity commitment and extra logging hooks (2–3 sprint delivery).
- Server-side long-lived keys: risky to de-gate. If CloudLane wants a hosted integration we can offer a token-exchange flow (short-lived tokens + rotation) instead of exposing long-lived keys. That may satisfy their use-case without opening a gate.
- Admin moderation hooks: probably the easiest to make partner-available behind an entitlement toggle after we ship the compliance sweep; ETA Nov 2028 as Evelyn said.

I'll prepare a technical appendix with the minimal infra changes and a rough cost/effort estimate (in dev-weeks). Evelyn — tagging you for the MOP timeline inputs.

Ben Carter
Sr. PM, Integrations | Redwood Inference
